However, ads still play in every episode you download for offline listening, even though your account shows an active paid subscription. Write an email to the platform's customer support team about this problem.

Request that the issue be fixed or that you receive a refund for the malfunctioning feature.
Ask for confirmation once the problem has been resolved.

academicDiscussion.professorPost: This week we're looking at how small groups negotiate shared resources in everyday settings. Picture a set of neighbors who share a courtyard or driveway used for parking, gardening, or informal gatherings. Some residents want the group to adopt a fixed weekly schedule assigning specific days or hours to each household, while others prefer to leave access first-come, first-served. Which approach do you think works better for neighbors sharing a space like this? Why?

studentPosts.name: Maya
studentPosts.post: I think a fixed schedule works best. Without one, whoever is most persistent or has the most free time ends up using the space the most, which isn't fair to neighbors with unpredictable schedules, like parents or shift workers. A weekly rotation guarantees everyone gets a turn, even if it feels less spontaneous.

studentPosts.name: Derek
studentPosts.post: I get Maya's point about fairness, but a rigid schedule ignores how differently people actually use the space. Most days nobody wants the courtyard at the same time anyway, so first-come, first-served lets neighbors use it when they actually need it instead of wasting an assigned slot they can't use that week.
